newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen bid $65-$66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen bid $65-$66 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were seen priced $68.00 per cwt by owners anticipating demand from packers who might be a little short on supply, several feedlot sources said.
Packers were expected to bid $65.00 to $66.00 following light sales at $67.00 late this week, they said.

About 3,000 head sold Friday at $67.00 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 1,500 in Kansas, also at $67.00. The sales were down $1.00 from the bulk of sales on Wednesday and down $2.00 from last week. Lower beef prices pulled fed cattle prices down, they said.
Fed cattle prices were not expected to be impacted by Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report. The report nearly matched pre-estimate averages in the three major categories.
USDA pegged on-feed supplies as of May 1 at 109.0 percent of a year ago, compared with the pre-report average analyst estimate of 109.6 percent.
April placements were put at 112.0 percent, down slightly from the average estimate of 113.9 percent and April marketings were 102 percent, up slightly from the average estimate of 101.0 percent.
